title: Multithreading on a single core
context: Does a single-core CPU support Java multithreading?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (1 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Yes. The operating system's scheduler switches the core between threads very quickly, so several threads make progress by taking turns. This is concurrency, not parallelism. The program is still correct on one core, and Java threads work the same way. Multithreading gives no speed-up for pure CPU work on one core, but it still helps with waiting on I/O.

points.title: Time slicing
points.why: The OS interleaves threads on one core, so multithreading works without extra cores.

points.title: Concurrency versus parallelism
points.why: One core gives concurrency. Only several cores give true parallel execution.
